pass: P26 — gemma4 native decode gap (release hold): mechanism
source_of_the_derivation: No new GPU time was needed to find the mechanism: the P24 native runs already carried METALJAX_DEBUG=1, so the compile-gate decisions and the per-program counters are in their logs.

mechanism.one_line: The gemma-lib decode step is the body of one dynamic while loop, and that body's compile gate is `by_cost = METALJAX_TRACE_BUDGET / BlockCost(body)` — integer division, so a body one unit over the budget gets ZERO and never compiles. Stage 1's sdpa recognizer fuses all 60 of the 31B's attention layers and its body costs 18888; the native recognizer, which analyses @main only, fuses none and the same body costs 20388 — 388 over the 20000 budget. So the native decode dispatches ~20388 tape entries per token instead of replaying one compiled graph, and pays a full mx::clear_cache() per token on top. Row 2 has the identical recognizer divergence and is unharmed only because 16306 is still 23 % under the budget: that is why the gap looks like it scales with model size.
mechanism.confirmed_by: One environment variable on the same frozen RC binary, METALJAX_TRACE_BUDGET=21000, forces the compile without the fusion and moves row 1 from 301.6 to 254.8 ms/tok — 1.244x -> 1.051x of Stage 1, exactly row 2's ratio, with the counters flipping from 0 compiled calls / 257 flushes / 129 clears to 128 / 1 / 1.

body_cost_derivation.how: Neither stack prints a while body's cost, but it prints the sampler main's, and a dynamic-bound while is charged trip=1024 x body (the pessimistic trip both stacks use). The decomposition is EXACT, not fitted: main_cost = 55 + 1024 * body_cost for both rows, with the same 55-unit loop overhead.

which_of_the_two_budgets_refuses_it.note: body_compile_max = min(by_cost, by_bytes). Isolating them shows this is NOT P23's byte gate and NOT P20's item 6 (a mischarge the plan should have discounted) — it is the op-count budget alone, acting on an honest count.
which_of_the_two_budgets_refuses_it.is_the_count_an_overcharge: No. 339.8 units/layer on BOTH rows, and the 31B genuinely has 60 layers. Unlike row 13 (E2B-int4, P20) where the gate was reading a dequant chain the qmm emit absorbs, there is nothing here to discount away.
which_of_the_two_budgets_refuses_it.is_the_budget_itself_tight: Its stated rationale (metal_lowering.cc:789, control.py:150) is the Metal live-buffer limit of ~499k; 20000 sits ~25x under that, and so does 20388.

the_gap_scales_with_depth_because_cost_i.layer_count_evidence: jit_init_cache results 240 vs 192 (4 cache tensors/layer); jit___call args 965 vs 773 (16 weight args/layer); moe candidate rejections 421 vs 337 (7 rank>=3 reduces/layer). All three give 60 and 48.

counters_that_confirm_it.source: per-program stats lines, P24 native runs. The counters reset per execute and there are three executes, one per sampler.chat: warmup (8 tokens), prefill (1), decode (128). Quoted below is the decode execute.

per_decode_token.reading: One compiled graph replay per token on the 12B with no eager flush at all (a compiled body never flushes inside itself); on the 31B, zero replays, two blocking eager flushes and one full return of the MLX buffer pool to the OS, every token.

counters_that_confirm_it.the_12B_body_traces_once_and_is_reused: its first execute (the 8-token warmup) reports compiles=1 compiled_calls=8, and the two later chats report compiles=0 with compiled_calls=1 and 128 — the trace is built once and replayed 137 times.
counters_that_confirm_it.reading: 128 compiled replays on the 12B against 0 on the 31B, and on the 31B ~2 eager flushes and ONE mx::clear_cache() per decode token (the RC binary's eager_flush returns the whole pool to the OS past METALJAX_FLUSH_CLEAR_MB=2048). A compiled body never flushes inside itself, which is why the 12B's count is 1 for the whole decode.

prefill_falls_off_the_same_cliff.corroboration: 31B prefill ratio 2372.5/1906.5 = 1.2444 and decode ratio 301.6/242.4 = 1.2442 — the same multiplicative mechanism on two independent measurements of the same transformer step.

hypotheses_ruled_out_with_evidence.output_copies_of_the_KV_cache: jit__sample_loop reports 246 output copies (31B) / 198 (12B), 0 donated — but it is executed 3 times in the whole run (once per sampler.chat), not once per token. The 128 tokens happen INSIDE one execute. Copies do not scale per token and are not in decode_ms_tok.
hypotheses_ruled_out_with_evidence.per_token_host_round_trips_or_transfers: ingest=0MB on both rows through decode; one executable per chat, not per token; both rows run the decode loop serial_loops=1 with loop_flushes=128, i.e. the SAME two host round trips per token. Equal on both stacks, so not the differentiator.
hypotheses_ruled_out_with_evidence.sdpa: SUPERSEDED by the measurement — see ROOT_CAUSE_measured. The pre-run arithmetic was right that the FUSION is timing-neutral at T=1 (P24, row 2) and wrong to conclude sdpa was not the cause: the recognizer's cost DISCOUNT is exactly what keeps Stage 1's body under the budget (1500 units on the 31B, 25.0 per attention, against 1112 units of headroom). The pre-run estimate of >=18 attentions needed was correct; the assumption that native could only ever find ~10 was not — Stage 1 finds all 60.
hypotheses_ruled_out_with_evidence.msl_scan: 0 msl plans on all three rows (P24 gate-1 requirement, verified there).
hypotheses_ruled_out_with_evidence.e2b_is_not_the_control_it_looks_like: manifest.json puts gemma4-e2b-bf16 on the keras_lm path, NOT gemma-lib. It is at parity for the same reason anyway: its body costs 12852 units, comfortably under the budget.

why_the_two_stacks_can_differ_at_all.same_formula_same_budget: Both stacks compute by_cost the same way from the same budget, so a divergence can only come from a different BlockCost — i.e. from a recognizer discount one stack takes and the other does not.
why_the_two_stacks_can_differ_at_all.known_divergence: Stage 1's sdpa analyses every function in the module (src/metaljax/sdpa.py::_all_blocks); the native one walks only @main and its nested regions (plugin-native/metal/metal_sdpa.cc::AnalyzeSdpa). This is the documented 'not ported by design: an sdpa or moe root living wholly inside a callee' (rc-gates-2026-08-16.md, known-and-accepted 2).
why_the_two_stacks_can_differ_at_all.status: OPEN — needs the Stage-1 side of the gate measured (queued as P26 R1/R3).

decomposition_of_the_gap.method: Decode on these rows is memory-bandwidth bound, so a stack that is doing the SAME kind of work on both rows must scale with model bytes. The 31B/12B byte ratio is 62.6/23.9 = 2.619.
decomposition_of_the_gap.reading: Stage 1's 31B sits exactly on the bandwidth line (0.99x); the native 31B carries a 17 % excess that its own 12B does not. The excess is confined to the row whose body fell off the gate.
decomposition_of_the_gap.prediction_basis: Stage 1's 242.4 x the 12B's own same-day native/Stage-1 ratio of 1.051 — i.e. assume the 31B would carry exactly the baseline native overhead the 12B does.
decomposition_of_the_gap.residual_reading: the same 1.051x baseline the 12B shows with both stacks compiled — not specific to this row
within_the_46_8_ms_two_costs_not_yet_spl: op-by-op dispatch of ~20388 tape entries per token instead of one compiled replay (no kernel fusion, per-entry executor work)

~2 eager flushes per token, one of which returns the whole MLX buffer pool to the OS (mx::clear_cache), measured at ~70 ms/clear on a different row in P20 — this half is what P25's in-flight change removes
decomposition_of_the_gap.12B_reading: both stacks compile the 12B body, so its 1.051x is the native stack's baseline overhead on this route and is NOT the same phenomenon.

why_extending_sdpa_would_not_fix_it.status: WRONG, and retracted — kept because the reasoning error is instructive.
why_extending_sdpa_would_not_fix_it.what_was_argued: That the body gate reads an unfused count, inferred from the two rows' decode bodies having the same cost per layer (339.7 vs 339.8) even though the 12B 'fires 8 attentions'.
why_extending_sdpa_would_not_fix_it.why_it_was_wrong: The premise was right and the conclusion inverted. Both decode bodies really do carry no discount — because NATIVE fuses zero attentions in either decode body; the 12B's 8 are in its prefill program. So the equality showed the divergence rather than ruling it out. Stage 1's own narration settles it: 48 and 60 fused attentions in those same two bodies.

R2_the_fix_probe_CONFIRMED.what: The SAME frozen RC binary (ed355691...94a16), one environment variable, nothing rebuilt: METALJAX_TRACE_BUDGET=21000.
R2_the_fix_probe_CONFIRMED.protocol: machine lock held (acquired after 760 s of waiting for the P25 campaign), settle + precheck claimed=10G swap=0G, guard budget 80 G / GUARD_RSS_GB=115 / system 100, one process, METALJAX_DEBUG=1.

memory.reading: compiling the body costs 1 GB of footprint on this row — it holds one iteration's intermediates instead of flushing inside it. Well inside the row's budget.

R2_the_fix_probe_CONFIRMED.the_prediction_was_exact: Before the run, 254.8 ms/tok was predicted as Stage 1's 242.4 x the 12B's own native/Stage-1 ratio of 1.051. Measured: 254.8. Both the decode and the prefill collapse from 1.244x to the 12B's 1.05x, i.e. the row stops being special.

ROOT_CAUSE_measured.what_stage1_sees_that_native_does_not: Stage 1's sdpa recognizer fuses EVERY attention layer in the gemma-lib decode body; the native one fuses none of them. Measured, both rows, from the stacks' own narration:

gemma4-31B_decode_body.reading: Stage 1 clears the 20000 budget by 5.9 % and ONLY because of that discount; without it, it too would be 388 units over.

gemma4-12B_decode_body.reading: the same divergence, but harmless: the unfused 16306 is still 22.7 % under the budget, which is why row 2 is only 1.05x.

ROOT_CAUSE_measured.correction_to_the_briefing: The '8 fused attentions on the 12B, 0 on the 31B' asymmetry is not what it looked like. Stage 1's narration shows the 12B's 8 are a Q=256 program (prefill, B1N16Q256K256D512) — the DECODE body (B1N8Q2K1024D256) is 48 on Stage 1 and 0 on native. So native fuses ZERO attentions in the decode body of BOTH rows; the rows differ only in whether the resulting cost clears the budget.
ROOT_CAUSE_measured.why_native_finds_none: The fused lowering analyses @main only — metal_lowering.cc:6684-6689 calls AnalyzeQmm/AnalyzeMoe/AnalyzeSdpa on `main` and nothing else, while Stage 1's sdpa.analyze walks _all_blocks (every function in the module). This is the documented 'not ported by design: an sdpa or moe root living wholly inside a callee' (rc-gates-2026-08-16.md, known-and-accepted 2). The gemma-lib sampler puts its decode step inside a callee.

measured_arms.protocol: machine lock per run, settle + precheck, guard 80 G / GUARD_RSS_GB=115 / system 100 (45 G for the 12B), one process per arm, METALJAX_DEBUG=1 throughout, native arms on the frozen RC dylib ed355691...94a16 (hash re-verified before the runs). Logs ~/.cache/metaljax-bench/logs/p26-gemma-gap/.

split_of_the_59_2_ms_per_token.note: The first two exist only because the body did not compile: a compiled body never flushes inside itself, so it never reaches the clear. The third is the 1.051x row 2 shows with both stacks compiled.

memory.reading: compiling the body costs +1 GB; disabling the clear costs +1 GB. Neither approached the guard.

measured_arms.caveat_on_the_stage1_arms: R1/R3 (Stage 1, DEBUG=1, run back-to-back behind other 60 GB rows) read 97.2 and 255.6 against P24's clean 93.8 and 242.4 — 3.6 % and 5.4 % high, the suite-context trap plus the debug narration. Their VALUE here is the narration (sdpa counts and costs), not the timing; every ratio above uses P24's clean Stage-1 cells. The native arms are like-for-like with P24's 301.6: same binary, same debug setting, same guard, same protocol.

queued_measurements.status: ALL FOUR RAN — see measured_arms. R1 Stage-1 12B, R2 native 31B budget 21000, R3 Stage-1 31B, R4 native 31B clear off.
queued_measurements.protocol: ~/.cache/metaljax-bench/logs/p26-gemma-gap/p26_run.sh — lock FIRST then settle (a precheck before the lock only reads the other campaign's working set), never removes a lock that looks stale, GUARD_RSS_GB=115 / footprint 80 / system 100 for row 1 per P24.

why_this_is_not_a_contained_fix.the_knob_is_shared_by_construction: METALJAX_TRACE_BUDGET is read identically by both stacks (src/metaljax/ops/control.py:155 and plugin-native/metal/metal_lowering.cc:801), and engine.py:455 records why: the compile decision is what the two engines must agree on above all. Raising it in plugin-native alone would make the native lowering take a compile decision Stage 1 refuses on the same program — a divergence the tape diff exists to catch.
why_this_is_not_a_contained_fix.and_src_is_frozen_this_era: A correct fix therefore edits src/metaljax/ops/control.py as well, which this era's rules freeze. So the default cannot be changed here; it is Oleg's call.
why_this_is_not_a_contained_fix.zero_code_mitigation_that_keeps_the_stac: METALJAX_TRACE_BUDGET=21000 in the environment — a documented user knob (notes/env-flags.md), read by both stacks, no rebuild. The smallest round value clearing both the 20388-unit decode body and the 20839-unit prefill call.
options_for_Oleg: Do nothing: ship 0.11.4 with row 1 at 301.6 and the mechanism documented; the row is 1.27x of the 0.11.3 anchor and this is why.

Document the knob in the release notes for models deeper than ~58 layers on this route. Row 1 is the whole published exposure today: the gemma-lib sampler is what puts an entire transformer step inside ONE dynamic while body, so it is the route where a per-layer cost of 340 units meets a 20000-unit ceiling. Row 9 (R1-Distill-32B) is deeper still at 64 layers and sits at 0.98x of its anchor, because manifest.json puts it on the keras_lm path, whose decode is a sequence of small executables rather than one big body.

Raise the default in BOTH stacks (reopens src/). The stated rationale for 20000 — the ~499k Metal live-buffer limit — has ~25x headroom, but the budget also sizes the eager flush cadence, so it wants a memory ladder of its own.

Soften the cliff rather than move it: `by_cost = budget / cost` going to 0 costs the body its compile AND its chunked replay at once, so a body 2 % over the line falls all the way to op-by-op. Nothing intermediate exists.

interaction_with_the_concurrent_P25_work.what: P25's uncommitted plugin-native/runtime/program.cc replaces the eager flush's mx::clear_cache() with a cache-limit bound set once at client construction.
interaction_with_the_concurrent_P25_work.why_it_matters_here: On row 1 that clear fires ~once per decode token (129 clears / 128 tokens) purely BECAUSE the body is uncompiled; on row 2 it fires once for the whole decode. So P25's change removes one of the two per-token costs on row 1 without touching the root cause (the body still dispatches ~20388 tape entries per token instead of replaying one compiled graph).
interaction_with_the_concurrent_P25_work.consequence: Row 1 should be re-measured after P25 lands, independently of this finding — the 301.6 cell was taken on a binary that clears the pool once per token on this row.

token_streams.measured: greedy token ids, 64 compared, all against P24's clean Stage-1 run
token_streams.reading: All three native arms diverge from Stage 1 at the SAME index and agree with each other, so row 1's token divergence is NOT the compile decision — forcing the body to compile does not move it. It is the recognizer divergence itself: native computes attention unfused in every arm while Stage 1 fuses all 60. That matches P24's observation that row 1's divergence is reproducible (unlike rows 5/7, where the fused path is nondeterministic run to run) — here it is the UNFUSED path that is stable.
token_streams.consequence_for_the_root_fix: If the callee-aware recognizer were ported, row 1's native stream should become Stage-1-identical (as rows 2 and 4 already are). That is a clean acceptance criterion for the fix, and also a warning: it changes the published stream for this row.
